perplexity.description:
Stick Around For Joy, released in February 1992 on the One Little Indian label, is the third and final studio album by The Sugarcubes, an Icelandic rock band known for their distinctive blend of alternative pop and rock. The album features a polished, upbeat sound characterized by punchy production and shimmering, funky pop elements, showcasing Björk's unique and urgent vocal style prominently. It includes notable singles such as "Hit," which reached number one on the US Modern Rock charts, and "Leash Called Love," which topped the US Dance Chart.

Musically, the album continues the band's exploration of eclectic, danceable rock with a mix of free-floating keyboards, splashy drums, and playful vocal interplay, maintaining the quirky yet accessible style that defined their earlier work. While it did not achieve the same critical acclaim or commercial success as their debut Life's Too Good (1988), Stick Around For Joy was better received than their sophomore album and helped solidify the band's legacy before their breakup later in 1992. The album peaked at number 95 on the Billboard 200 and number 16 on the UK Albums Chart, marking the band's lowest chart positions but still reflecting a dedicated following.
